You read transcripts of Bitcoin videos. For each EXCERPT below, the sentences inside <selected> are a clip
that may be shown on its own. Use the whole excerpt (what comes before and after) to judge the selected words. You do
not know how the clip will be used.

<excerpt label="M" channel="Stephan Livera" video_title="Joe Burnett: Your Wealth Is Melting in the Age of AI | SLP788" published="2026-11-11T18:03" show_date="2026-11-12">Today would be a great time to just talk a bit about the thesis for Bitcoin because I think sometimes people can kind of lose sight of the fundamentals sometimes. So maybe just offer an initial comment on your kind of broad macro view and what you're seeing in terms of Bitcoin sentiment. Yeah, absolutely. I mean, I think it's very important to go back to the fundamentals of Bitcoin in times like this, right? I'm reminded of a current, you know, negative aspect of framing Bitcoin right now where people will say, oh, Bitcoin's five -year return is practically zero, which is factually correct. If you happen to have bought Bitcoin at the November of 2021 and held it to today, and if you bought the exact peak, you would have bought it around $69,000 per Bitcoin. Today, Bitcoin's at $73,000 per Bitcoin, and you had... pretty much a 0 % return. But I'm reminded of what actually happened at the bottom of the 2022 Bitcoin bear market, where literally the exact same argument was being used, where, okay, from the peak in 2020, 2017, which was around like $20,000 per Bitcoin, Bitcoin in 2022, it was actually below $20,000. Like I think it was $16,000, $15,000. was the low back in 2022. So that was like a, you know, a 20, 25 % a negative return over five years for Bitcoin. <selected>That's terrible.</selected> But of course, in hindsight, that was like the ideal time to load up on additional Bitcoin. So yeah, I mean, I think like, one Bitcoin is an incredibly, incredibly volatile asset. Like the bull markets are insane. The bear markets are brutal and can be devastating if you don't have the right time horizon. And if you weren't. expecting the volatility. But ultimately, I think Bitcoin is objectively the best form of money that humanity is ever discovered. It has these unique monetary properties, scarcity, portability, durability, durability, divisibility, divisibility, and fungibility that make Bitcoin a better form of money. And this volatility is just normal market processes, trying to grok and understand what Bitcoin is. Sometimes everyone... loves it because the price is going up. Sometimes everyone hates it because there's another hot investment at the time or the price just hasn't cooperated for a certain period of time and people lose interest.</excerpt>

For each excerpt answer:
- "speaker_changes_inside": does the speaker change inside the selected words? "yes" / "no" / "uncertain"
- "view": whose view the selected words express: "own_sincere" (the speaker's own sincere assertion), "attributed"
  (someone else's view, quoted or reported), "hypothetical", "conditional" (true only under a condition), "sarcastic",
  "question", "reading_aloud" (reading a post or article), "ad_read", "joke", or "uncertain"
- "referents": every pronoun or pointing word in the selected words (it, they, this, that, he, she, today, here...)
  that points at something specific, with what it refers to; "inside": true if the selected words themselves give
  its antecedent or the predicate that completes it (an ellipsis completed by an earlier selected sentence: "It's not
  Bitcoin that's getting hacked. It's other intermediaries." = other intermediaries are getting hacked), or it points
  only at a general topic the clip presupposes; "inside": false if a listener needs the words before or after the
  selection; "changes_assertion": "yes" if resolving it differently would change WHAT THE SPEAKER ASSERTS, "no" if
  not, "uncertain". Leave out words that point at nothing outside: a dummy "it" ("it's raining", "it's not X that
  ...", where X is in the selection), and a generic "we" / "you" / "they" meaning people in general
- "conditions": any condition or time frame that governs the selected words, and whether it is INSIDE them
- "retraction": "none", or what the speaker later in the excerpt retracts or qualifies about the selected words
- "time_ok": "yes" if every time word in the selected words (today, now, this week, just, recently, a "current"
  price) still holds on the show date given when the video was published (both on the excerpt), or there is none;
  "no" if it is stale; "uncertain"
- "proposition": in one sentence, what the speaker asserts in the selected words, read in context
- "certainty": "certain", "likely", "possible", "speculative" or "uncertain"
- "speaker_is": "host" if the excerpt shows that the speaker of the selected words is the channel's own host,
  "guest" if it shows a guest or another person speaking them, "uncertain" otherwise; "speaker_evidence": the exact
  words of the excerpt that show it (copied exactly, e.g. the host's own "welcome back to my channel"), or ""
